title: Josephus Survivor
statement: There are n people numbered 1 through n standing in a circle. Starting from person 1, count k people and remove the kth, repeating from the next person until one survivor remains. Print the survivor's one-based label. Inputs satisfy n>=1 and k>=1. Use the standard zero-based recurrence and convert back to one-based numbering at the end. Input and output must follow the examples exactly. Print only the requested result and no labels. The reference implementation is intended for the full constraints, while the brute-force implementation is suitable for small cases and serves as an independent comparison. Respect case sensitivity, ordering, multiplicity, and empty-input behavior as defined above.
input_format: Read the text, integer, or parameter lines described in the statement.
output_format: Print the requested value or transformed string in the specified format.
constraints: String length and numeric values fit standard contest limits; range queries have a manageable width; n is within 200000 where applicable.
reference_python:
import sys
n,k=map(int,sys.stdin.read().split());r=0
for i in range(1,n+1):r=(r+k)%i
print(r+1)
brute_force_python:
import sys
n,k=map(int,sys.stdin.read().split());p=list(range(1,n+1));i=0
while len(p)>1:i=(i+k-1)%len(p);p.pop(i)
print(p[0])
